Bank and fork-tree state management for Solana runtime, with CoW pools and locks.

# Purpose
`fd_bank.h` defines the bank state model used by the runtime to track Solana block execution in memory. It declares the `fd_bank_t` type, which stores per-block runtime data such as slot numbers, hashes, fee data, epoch data, sysvar cache data, and execution counters. The file also defines the `fd_banks_t` manager, which owns a pool of banks and keeps the fork tree in a left-child, right-sibling form so the runtime can create child banks, query banks by bank index, advance the root, and prune dead or rooted branches. The design is fork-aware and uses bank indices instead of slot numbers so the code can handle equivocation, where more than one block can exist for the same slot.

The file also defines the memory and concurrency model for bank fields. Some fields are stored directly inside `fd_bank_t`, while CoW fields such as `epoch_rewards`, `epoch_leaders`, and vote state caches use separate pools and per-field locks. The header provides inline helpers to join and leave pools, query and modify fields with or without locks, and manage the delta-based `stake_delegations` state and the pooled `cost_tracker`. It also declares the main bank lifecycle APIs, including `fd_banks_new`, `fd_banks_init_bank`, `fd_banks_new_bank`, `fd_banks_clone_from_parent`, `fd_banks_advance_root_prepare`, `fd_banks_advance_root`, `fd_banks_mark_bank_dead`, `fd_banks_mark_bank_frozen`, and `fd_banks_validate`.
